notes: All headline numbers reproduce to the last printed digit; rounding to 4 dp is exact. EXPERIMENTAL MEAN: 86.9446040516 -> 86.9446 as claimed. CONFOUNDS FOUND (none invalidate the claim): (a) the experimental values include 82 exact integers and only 284 distinct values (ties), and 49/543 reference values are rounded integers, so MAE has substantial discreteness; (b) 331/543 observations have an exact (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) row in bde_db_full.csv.gz; on those the matched DB bde gives MAE 1.8370 (corr 0.999 with the quantum channel) - a different, slightly better number, so the 'quantum' channel is a recalibrated/perturbed version of the DB value, not the raw DB row; the reference channel matches the DB bde on 0 rows (corr 0.93); (c) the quantum-vs-learned gap (-0.3129 MAE, 5000-draw bootstrap 95% CI [-0.4661,-0.1649], P(diff>0)=0.000) is statistically clear but an order of magnitude smaller than the quantum-vs-reference gap, so '2.4107 vs 2.0978' should not be over-read. POOLED-VARIANCE CHECK (claim 11, independent): the correct pooled within-molecule SD is sqrt(sum_g (n_g-1)s_g^2 / sum_g(n_g-1)) = 9.965372 (rounds to the claimed 9.97) over 86 multi-row molecules, 419 unique molecules, mean/median/max within-molecule spread 13.4186/11.90/47.90 (claim says 13.42/11.90/47.9 - all match). The ~165 figure is NOT an ordinary naive pooled formula: ddof-0 n-weighted pooling gives 10.110236 and unweighted mean-of-variance gives 10.315528, while sqrt(sum of variances) over groups gives 95.66. The exact 165.2622713320976 is reproduced only by squaring the per-group variances inside the weighted average, sqrt( avg( s_g^2 SQUARED, weights=n_g-1 ) ) = 165.2622713321 (match to 1e-9). That slip is present in the original code at output/analysis/ws5_het.py line 24 ('np.average((var.to_numpy(float))**2, weights=...)'), confirming 165 is a var-squared artifact, not a weighting/ddof artifact.
